tier_reason: README Benchmarks tables compare chili against rayon::join and a sequential baseline on a balanced-tree sum, with CPU models stated and bench code in the repo (Cargo.toml [[bench]] overhead, divan + rayon dev-deps), but no compiler version or flags are given, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Ryzen 7 4800HS 8 cores: 1023 nodes 3.4 us vs Rayon 51.1 us; 16.7M nodes 13.6 ms vs 58.1 ms; 134M nodes 101.8 ms vs 497.2 ms. Apple M1: 1023 nodes 3.5 us vs 29.2 us; 16.7M nodes 11.2 ms vs 40.5 ms; 67.1M nodes 44.3 ms vs 167.1 ms. At 1023 nodes chili is slower than the sequential baseline (1.8 us, x0.53 on Ryzen; 1.6 us, x0.46 on M1).
corrections.caveats: Single synthetic tree-sum benchmark; compiler and flags not stated; Rust port of Spice. At 1K nodes both chili and Rayon are slower than the single-threaded baseline (chili x0.53 / x0.46), so the win over Rayon there is overhead reduction, not a speedup over sequential code. Found via HN thread 'Show HN: Chili' title only (thread blocked).

notes: Numbers match the README. License MIT OR Apache-2.0 confirmed via Cargo.toml plus LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE files (no plain LICENSE). Last commit 2025-05-01, 721 stars confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: README Benchmarks section shows a nanobench MSVC table (code in ./benchmark, CPU Ryzen 7 5800X stated) against BS::thread_pool, task_thread_pool and riften::Thiefpool, but compiler version and flags are not given; first-party, margins within a few percent, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Own MSVC table (256x256 matmul, relative to dp::thread_pool with std::function): dp std::function 93.27 ms/op (100%), dp std::move_only_function 90.66 ms/op (102.9%), dp fu2::unique_function 94.50 ms/op (98.7%), BS::thread_pool 99.73 ms/op (93.5%), task_thread_pool 91.29 ms/op (102.2%), riften::Thiefpool 93.18 ms/op (100.1%). README says it is faster than other thread pool libraries in most cases, but riften pulls ahead in some cases and task_thread_pool with many small tasks.
corrections.caveats: Margins against BS::thread_pool are about 7 percent; task_thread_pool beats the std::function variant and riften ties it; one workload only; run on Windows with frequency scaling noted by the author; compares against other small thread pools, not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon; compiler version and flags not stated. Repo now lives at github.com/ptsouchlos/thread-pool (old DeveloperPaul123 URL redirects).

notes: Repo was renamed/moved to ptsouchlos/thread-pool; README CPM snippet uses that path. MIT license, 568 stars, last commit 2026-09-10 confirmed. Clang results file linked in README was not opened.

tier_reason: README shows an example run of benchmark/benchmark.cpp (job reposting, 16 concurrent chains of 1,000,001 reposts) against an author-written boost::asio io_service pool (benchmark/asio_thread_pool.hpp); no compiler, flags or CPU given, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Reposting 1,000,001 jobs in 61.7-70.3 ms vs 1,381.6-1,393.2 ms for the boost::asio io_service based pool (about 20x, derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Not compared against TBB, OpenMP or Rayon; baseline is an author-written asio io_service pool with a single shared queue, while reposting from a worker hits that worker's own queue, so the benchmark favors the work-distribution design. README gives no compiler, flags or CPU. MPMCBoundedQueue is under Vyukov's BSD-2-Clause terms (OSI-approved). The yvoinov/thread-pool-cpp fork reports the same numbers.

notes: The separately licensed part turned out to be BSD-2-Clause, so usability moves from mixed to copyable. Last commit 2018-02-06 ('Fix multiple link units'), 585 stars, not archived.
